outcome.technical:
ONE MODULE: every CI-run bug is filed by full-gate.py (record_ci_run -> file_ci_bug); the call site removed is drive-phase.py ci_file_red and its audit-task.py bug-add (cib1 holds it). full-gate.py --ci-run reads the run's CORE (databaseId,headSha,headBranch,status,conclusion,url) and, for a red run only, the jobs in a second gh call; jobs gh cannot list are said in the bug in gh's words (bounded by _output.clip_bytes, 200 bytes, marked '...') and never refuse the run. The record goes through _evidence_io.write_plan_file under the index lock after revalidating the plan with it in place (_manifest_rules.bound_validator). --ci-unreported SHA --phase P --basis [--run RUNID] records a run not listed, or listed and not readable. EXITS of the two flags: 0 recorded/already recorded; 1 the record refused (plan would not validate; the words name validate-manifest, /audit:bug and taking ci.cadence out), not written (plan lock: the words name the rerun or the lock command), or a red run's bug verb failed (record stands; the words say a rerun files it); 2 usage (points at --help); 6 E_UNREAD, the core could not be read, nothing written (the words name the rerun and --ci-unreported --run). 6 is unused by full-gate.py and above _locks' 3/4/5; COMPATIBILITY.md promises no exit code but the validators' (section 'Not promised': 'every exit code except the validators''), so moving the unreadable run from 1 to 6 breaks no promise. STATE TABLE (full-gate.py docstring; known / phase.ci / exit / what the drive does and shows): concluded -> runId,sha,conclusion,at / 0 / did-line 'CI : recorded run N (c) on P.ci', run released [fgci4,fgci7,wv10]; red -> + one bug unless its title exists / 0 / did-line '...; filed a high bug' [fgci1,wv9]; red, jobs unread -> + bug saying they could not be read, gh's words / 0 / did-line '...; filed a high bug, its failed jobs unread' [fgci13]; green -> jobs never asked [fgci14]; same run again -> nothing / 0 / did-line 'already recorded...none filed' [fgci2,wv9b]; not concluded -> runId,sha,at,basis(status), never a conclusion / 0 / at a close not asked, did-line 'still running'; at the commit recorded [fgci5, drive unit]; not listed at the commit -> sha,at,basis / 0 / goes on [fgci6, drive unit]; list unreadable (no gh, logged out, 502) at the commit -> sha,at,basis quoting gh / 0 / goes on [cic1]; at a close or sign-off begin -> did-line 'CI unread: ', nothing [cic1]; listed, core unreadable at the commit -> runId,sha,at,basis naming which read failed and gh's words, no conclusion / 0 via --ci-unreported --run / goes on [cic2,fgci12]; at a close -> did-line 'unread: run N: ...', run held [cic2]; core unreadable -> nothing / 6 [fgci3,fgci10,fgci15]; record refused -> nothing / 1 / stop: full-gate's words, then the 'stopped' rule, then CI_WAY_ON ('The drive reads this run again at the next `next`; to go on without CI's word, take `ci.cadence` out of the audit config.') [fgci9,cic3]; lock -> nothing / 1 / same stop; usage -> nothing / 2 / same stop [fgci11,cic3]; CI not configured or never pushed -> absent / no verb [cis2]. SIGN-OFF STOP: a missing or unauthenticated gh at sign-off no longer stops or drops anything: the commit carries a record with a basis quoting gh. The sign-off stops only on a refused record, a usage error or the plan lock; the person sees '[drive-phase] P: stopped - full-gate.py refused (exit N); its own words follow', the verb's line naming its repair, 'Relay these words and act on the remedy they name...', and CI_WAY_ON. No answer is open at that stop; the next `next` re-runs finish_signoff and reads again, and removing ci.cadence (ci_before_signoff returns None without it) goes on. READERS OF phase.ci (grep after the last edit: get('ci')/['ci'] over scripts, hooks, .claude/hooks and tools; 'ci' strings under status, report, panel, ui and guard-release.py): full-gate.py itself YES (_put_ci reads the stored record to tell 'the same run read again' from a replacement); the drive NO (its state.get('ci') is its own .claude/state file); release guard NO; status NO; report NO; panel NO (_panel_settings 'ci' is the config settings group id); doctor NO; lookup NO. Nothing outside the verb reads the key. RESIDUE (not fixed): after the sign-off commit nothing reads CI again, so a run that concludes red after sign-off, or whose core could not be read at the commit, reaches the plan as a record with a basis and no bug. Before this task it was the same: nothing read CI after sign-off, and an unread list at sign-off was a did-line with nothing filed; now the gap is at least recorded in the plan. That is the question for the task that makes a landing wait for CI.
